Descriptions.DescriptionText: This is a PvE server. Please keep encounters with other players friendly: no shooting on sight or non-consensual player kills.
High-value loot locations are heavily guarded by armed patrols. Come prepared with weapons, ammunition, and medical supplies.

Approximately every one to two hours, a hostile aircraft may fly over a player. When you receive an incoming-aircraft warning, take cover and stay out of sight. If the aircraft spots you, it will deploy hostile paratroopers to hunt players in the area.
Airborne AI reinforcement flares can be found as loot around the map. Load one into a flare gun and fire it to call a friendly reinforcement aircraft to your location.

The friendly aircraft will fly overhead and deploy friendly AI reinforcements near the location where the flare was fired. Approach the reinforcements and use the Recruit action on them. Once recruited, they will follow you and assist you in combat.
Remember the difference: hide from unrequested hostile aircraft, but remain near your reinforcement flare so you can locate and recruit the friendly troops it calls.

Locked loot rooms are marked permanently on the Expansion map. Press M to view them. Green markers are Tier 1 rooms, orange markers are Tier 2 rooms, and red markers are Tier 3 rooms. Tier 2 and Tier 3 markers also name the room's weapon theme.

There are three functional keycards and three access tiers. Keycard 01 opens Tier 1 rooms, Keycard 02 opens Tier 2 rooms, and Keycard 03 opens Tier 3 rooms. A door's physical appearance does not necessarily indicate its access tier; trust the room's map marker. There is no functional Tier 4 card or room.

A keycard is consumed when it is swiped. Opening the door creates a temporary reward crate inside the room. Take everything you want before the door closes, because the crate is removed when the door shuts.

Tier 1 rooms always provide one early-game primary weapon bundle: MP5-K, UMP45, PP-19, AKS-74U, or Saiga, with a rare chance of a full AK-74 instead. Most bundles include a spare magazine, a sight where it fits, and several boxes of ammunition.

Every Tier 1 crate includes a combat knife and has independent bonus chances for a sidearm kit (FNX45 25 percent, CZ 75 20 percent, engraved M1911 10 percent), a frag grenade (25 percent), a ballistic helmet (15 percent), and an 8 percent chance of a Keycard 02 to take you up to Tier 2.

Each of the three Tier 2 rooms has its own theme, shown on its map marker, so you can target the weapon you want. Each Tier 2 crate provides two different weapon bundles from that room's pool, with a spare magazine and two boxes of ammunition.
Tier 2 Marksman room (northwest of Vybor, near Lopatino): SV-98, VSS, SKS with PU scope, or M16A2 with ACOG. Always includes a rangefinder.
Tier 2 CQB / SMG room (Grishino area): P90, AS VAL, AUG Short, or Benelli M4. Any one of these has a 50 percent chance per crate. Also has a 50 percent chance of a pair of flashbangs.
Tier 2 Assault Rifle room (Vybor area): AKM, AK-101, AUG, FAMAS, TAR-21, or ADAR Modular 16.

Every Tier 2 crate also has independent bonus chances for a pair of frag grenades (35 percent), a plate carrier (15 percent), an MMG JPC vest (10 percent), NV goggles (5 percent), and a 6 percent chance of a Keycard 03.

Tier 3 rooms provide one high-end weapon bundle from a pool unique to each site, with a spare magazine, scope where appropriate, and extra ammunition. The Tisy Heavy room offers SCAR-H, M4A1 with a 60-round magazine, SNAFU AWM, or RPD.
The MB Kamensk Precision room offers FAL, M14, Gevar Black, or SVD. Each site has exclusive weapons, giving you a reason to visit both.

Every Tier 3 crate has independent bonus chances for NV goggles (30 percent), an M79 grenade launcher with explosive and smoke rounds (20 percent), and a plate carrier (40 percent). Heavy crates add a pair of frag grenades (50 percent) and an MMG TT vest (25 percent). Precision crates add a ghillie suit with hood (35 percent) and always include a rangefinder.

Many Rating 3 and Rating 4 military items have been removed from ordinary map loot, although selected weapons can still appear very rarely at dynamic events. Keycard rooms are the dependable progression path to these equipment tiers.

Cards 01 and 02 can appear in military world loot and on police or army infected. Card 03 is not carried by police or ordinary army infected. It has only a very small natural military-loot population in map tiers 3 and 4.

The main route to Card 03 is the hostile AI force at Northwest Airfield. Eligible regular soldiers have a small chance to drop one, while the airfield sniper has a much higher chance. AI equipment itself cannot be looted; check the controlled rewards dropped beside defeated patrol members.

Northwest Airfield is the bridge to Tier 3, not the final reward destination. Survive the airfield, obtain Card 03, then travel to Tisy or MB Kamensk for their exclusive weapon pools. A card is consumed on use, so obtaining another lets you pursue the other site's weapons.
Room markers show the destination but the map does not show your player position, coordinates, or distance to the room. Navigate using landmarks and normal compass skills.

A keycard door remains open for 180 seconds, followed by a 15-second closing delay. The alarm is disabled, so there is no audible warning. Keep track of your time and leave the room before the door shuts.
The room can be used by anyone while its door is open.
